newsitem.title: FRANCE: CIC boss to offer privatisation plan soon.
newsitem.headline: CIC boss to offer privatisation plan soon.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Monday he would meet CIC boss Philippe Pontet in the coming weeks and Pontet was expected to present proposals for privatising the regional bank grouping.

Arthuis called off a CIC privatisation tender on November 14 after getting just two offers, from BNP and Societe Generale, of which only the former had been judged eligible by France's independent Privatisation Commission.
He said the privatisation would go ahead after a rethink and asked the heads of the 13 regional banks which make up the CIC group to draw up proposals.
Arthuis told a news conference in this northeastern town that he expected to meet Pontet "in the coming weeks".
He said privatisation would have to respect the interests of CIC's parent company, state-owned insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN) and those of the regions in which CIC is based.
Arthuis, on a visit to the northeastern Alsace region, was due to meet a staff delegation on Monday afternoon from Cial, the CIC bank in the region.

Pontet took over as head of CIC after the departure of Bernard Yoncourt, who infuriated Arthuis during the now-defunct sale tender by saying the possible forms of privatisation in the pipeline could spell the death of the CIC grouping.

Yoncourt was pushed out at the same time as GAN chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud was fired by the government and replaced by Didier Pfeiffer. The government justified the firing of Bonnaud on the grounds that he failed to promote the CIC privatisation.
